en: Among the Chinese he became a lofty figure,
He was skilled at finding stratagems,
By making inquiries, he found a people,
The khan heeded the words of the inquiry,
He became a rumor among the Chinese,
That one who went from the Kyrgyz,
To the young champion of the in-laws,
They mounted him on an unbeatable pacer,
They dressed him in silk no bullet could pierce,
Among the Chinese people of twenty khans,
Making it known with a smiling face,
He had seen the brave men boast,
The two reins and a single lead-rope,
In Suurgan's time, it was bestowed.
Making the Blue Dörböt into a people,
He brought turmoil upon the Kalmyks,
The reins of all Beijing,
He received from Tüp Teñir,
He took it from the people by the armful.
Calling Suurgan the great Blue Khan,
Calling him a singular, contented soul,
He ruled with surpassing authority,
The khans who spoke at one time,
He slaughtered several of them.
Seeing his awesome might, Tüp Teñir,
Gave it to his Kalmyk people,
Placing the Ayran crown upon him,
Carefully seating him upon the throne,
Giving him a beard and mastery,
His land for a day, his day for the world,
Giving night to his due,
Seating the remaining one on the throne,
Giving him rule over the khagan's people,
Saying his spiritual power reached afar,
Frightening all of Beijing,
The Kalmyk called Azyrky,
Putting the Jan cap upon him,
Wherever he went, did he not act as a governor?
Was he not the one called Cold-Tongued?
A sixty-headed dragon,
The women beneath him,
From the weary black treasure,
His true nature from himself,
He had Khan Suurgan taught,
He held his white standard,
A Chinese soul studied here,
The khan gathered his resolve.
The son of Khan Suurchulgan,
Who had come and stood here,
Safe and sound, remaining upright,
He directed his people toward one course,
Arka Kongoz, the scourge of the foe,
What he drove was different, on the returning day,
Do not ask about his waters,
He set straight whichever way he looked,
When he spoke, [the final phrase is uncertain],
Oylok once witnessed it,
He remained deep in thought for a long time,
He saw one who had complained,
He learned it from the knowledgeable one,
Seeing the affair, he laughed,
When he showed his might, they recoiled in fear,
The baltyrkan in the brocade,
His noble word flashed brightly,
To the very root of the Türchü,
My breeze that turned back the kai,
Of the long-eared black one,
A master who knew skillful speech,
Of the heroes, [the epithet is uncertain],
His heart ranged broadly between them,
When he looked, his eyes were clear,
Of the word that stood firm as stone,
Even if sorrow came without remainder,
Say nothing against the khan's decree,
How could he make it small?
From a benefit worthy of the blood-price,
The commander of a thousand chosen from a myriad,
He thinned the people of Böz,
He drove back the people of Karagan,
Without turning back the enemy's champion,
Saying, 'What sort is the duldul steed?'
Seeing what manner of beauty it was,
Suurgan, from Khan Tengir,
The khan does not know his elder sister,
How many souls stood watching,
All of them despairing of life,
To the half with the crooked mouth,
The ruler gathered an army,
The hero Orokulon,
Let me set down the sorrow,
From Safat, toward the battle,
Was it right, meeting the enemy,
The one who would guard the prison,
Kudarman, the good sultan,
His close one who had seen much,
A hero skilled in wisdom,
The warrior who drew toward the moon,
From the clear-eyed, handsome one,
From the one who drove the sheep,
For the hundred, Kurman's division,
From his blue fortress itself,
Without turning back, he had them swept away,
When we look, it is a wondrous deed,
Leaving none behind, he would send the youths,
The forty gates of Beijing,
Making all their horses cry out,
At each gate, forty of their own,
Binding them in fetters and having them dragged,
Into the dark ravine of the world,
Forward, a courier to the thousand,
All of them descended and entered,
The one before was hardened,
The khan called the frightened hero,
They descended from his side,
Many people had a Sorko-like mouth,
Suurchulgan and Khan Tekür,
Who appointed the Kara Tüyкө,
The driver who took them on without turning back,
The whetstone of this Karagut,
His Alcha land was lacking,
From Düyshömük's benefit,
May God grant it—do not show it,
A shepherd soul amid beasts and thousands,
Cowards whose hearts are water,
Little lords who know no stratagem,
Saying he would die with no support,
The true battlefield from which none turns back,
Saying he stood and saw without yielding,
Wretches whose courage is scant,
Their heads patched, their legs splayed,
Wretches who know little,
One good man is worth a thousand bad,
On a dark road, light is good,
On the courageous path, ardor is good,
Saying he had seen its state to the bitter end,
At his right side was Munkara,
Do not ask about his Munkara,
He placed a letter at his door,
Calling out, 'Iri-müyrü,'
He gave the name Angsayyn,
The reason he gave that name,
Was to speak of the hero's breaking,
Wretches who know no master,
Making it still in his hand,
Its restraint lay in Bazdan's word,
His champions were extraordinary,
From the wretch who acted in a makeshift way,
Many of them from his onslaught,
A companion of human character,
Tumesho leaned upon his scabbard,
Your task concerned a man,
A soul standing there without a task,
Alas, no bend remained,
There is a mighty wrestler,
There is one who looks as though he took up a sword,
He grasped a spear and broke the horses' formation,
He has a flashing gun,
There is one whose bloodied face is wolf-like,
That one's venom was fierce,
There is one venomous as a dragon,
Khan, what fiery lowland is this?
Having seen flesh, he would sever the head,
What would he not do to stone!
He had often seen heads severed,
What is so very near?
You are no less than a dragon,
Like a cutting blow from Azar Kaysan,
At the word 'horse,' his riding seemed ready to launch,
As though Boshono could defend a thousand,
The one he encountered seemed fierce,
Whoever met him seemed doomed,
Enslaving whoever encountered him,
As though setting the burned one upon the ground,
A tower like a hero,
The Arab of the tower,
At the foot of the tower,
A lone white yurt stands below,
Two khans whose paths met,
Did no traveler come?
Someone is riding along at a steady pace,
This hero is Karakhan,
No one who saw it could remain standing,
Now it seems beyond all reach,
The tiger stands in fury,
The hapless one stands, unable to remain,
His fangs stand ready for torment,
The calamity this one has brought,
Have you seen it from this daughter of yours?
How many lands he drew troops against,
Striking him, the wicked black host,
Many are his raiding marches,
His great ones rode at the head,
The misery of those who cherish life,
He has a bone made for toil,
He burned it down to the roots,
Of the man who looked swiftly,
His heart was torn within him,
His teeth themselves are strong,
What is called his arm grew strong,
He satisfied the sorcerer,
Comparing him to Chubak's son,
Gathering without finding a champion,
Not building it for one unworthy,
Appearing mighty in courage,
A weak soul without courage,
He died before his destined hour,
Stirring bloodshed and gathering the people,
With his waters, truth descended,
The punishment of the Chinese people,
Have the third one delivered into their hands,
A khan's command is never twofold,
Is there anyone who will fight?
His courage is equal to three hundred,
Then his son stood there unharmed,
[Uncertain: Turning his eyes to the right,]
With sickle-curved brows,
[Uncertain: Sitting there himself in agitation,]
If you would see a marvel, look at this!
Gathering every last seer,
[Uncertain: He gathered those versed in hidden things,]
[Uncertain: If he would not give his judgment,]
If he would not obey what was said,
[Uncertain: He had made their blood run dark,]
[Uncertain: Hardship came upon their lives,]
Suurulgan, who had devised a plan,
When Suurulgan gave the order,
The teeming Kytai, the people of forty khans,
Were sorely distressed.
“Where will he drive us?” they wondered,
Fearing he would do such a deed again,
Bringing misery upon many people,
[Uncertain: Fearing he would slaughter them in punishment,]
His great wrath became apparent,
Even his valiant warriors,
Despairing of their precious lives,
All surged about in an uproar,
The army poured forth,
Their clamor rose to the sky.
All that was old was indeed old,
All that struck the stone was pierced,
Ear pressed against ear,
They moved in a swarm, clamoring like worms,
They asked what land and what kind it was,
Some souls went off in bewilderment,
Before long, some were astonished,
As he traveled among the people,
As he stood for the people,
In the royal city of Kökükö,
The people thronged and shone like ore,
On the blue hill stood a tower,
Do not ask about the tower,
If you ask about the tower,
In the khan’s land of China,
When the khan appeared before them,
When he was to issue an order,
The people clamored, the nation roared,
